newsitem.title: UK: Charter gains as Howden bid approved.
newsitem.headline: Charter gains as Howden bid approved.

text.p: Shares in Charter Plc rose on Friday, rebounding from recent weakness as the rail track equipment and welding products firm secured control of industrial ventilation group Howden Group Plc, dealers said.

Charter shares were up 10p at 792-1/2 by 0842 GMT in modest trade of 171,244 shares. The stock hit a year's high of 855p in the wake of the 378 million stg bid, launched on March 21, but quickly retreated to around the 775p level.
Charter said its bid won acceptances representing 66.6 percent of Howden shares, taking its total to 76.6 percent.

Traders said Charter's success in gaining control of Howden had probably lured some investors into the stock. "That is is obviously the reason," said one. "There were a couple of buy orders yesterday, it is good news for the company."
Another pointed out that the stock was due a bounce after recent weakness.
"There has been reasonably good volume for the last few days that has taken out all the loose holders," he said. "Having been oversold the buyers have come back in."
Announcing the agreed bid in March, Charter chairman and chief executive Jeffrey Herbert said the acquisition would boost earnings in its first year.
